content:
emma: Heads-up — Acme Health flagged a pretty confusing rerank result from /v1/batch_rerank. They sent two queries with distinct candidate lists but the response looks like candidates got flattened and scores applied to the wrong queries.

emma: Repro payload (sanitized):
```json
{
  "queries": [
    {"qid": "q-1", "candidates": ["c1", "c2"]},
    {"qid": "q-2", "candidates": ["d1"]}
  ]
}
```

emma: They got back: (response body simplified)
```json
{
  "request_id": "req_01GACDXYZ",
  "scores": [0.92, 0.81, 0.33],
  "mapping": null
}
```

emma: Notice 3 scores for a total of 3 candidates, but no per-query grouping or index mapping — which makes it impossible to tell whether the 3rd score is for q-1.c2 or q-2.d1. Customer says the top result moved from q-2 to q-1 after a second run.

jordan: Ack. Can you paste the raw response that includes headers? I want the x-request-id and any SDK metadata. Also which SDK version?

emma: Headers: `x-request-id: req_01GACDXYZ`, `x-sdk-version: redwood-python/1.12.0`, `x-model: rerank-mini-v2`. I'll attach a small dump.

liam: Do we have server logs for req_01GACDXYZ? I searched logs and found a warning around that time: `WARN: candidate_count(3) != per_query_expected(??)` — the code path that flattens per-query lists emits this when an internal flag is set.

ada: (from QA) we saw an SDK bug in 1.12.0 where the python client serializes multi-query candidate lists as a single flattened list if `flatten_candidates=true` env var is present. Did the customer set any env flags?

emma: Customer says they did not set env flags. They used the JSON body exactly like above. They called `POST /v1/batch_rerank` with `Content-Type: application/json`. No special headers except typical auth.

liam: Pasting server-side trace (sanitized):
```
2026-03-11T14:22:04.123Z INFO incoming request req_01GACDXYZ method=POST route=/v1/batch_rerank
2026-03-11T14:22:04.125Z DEBUG parsed_payload.queries = [{'qid':'q-1','candidates':['c1','c2']},{'qid':'q-2','candidates':['d1']}]
2026-03-11T14:22:04.127Z DEBUG serializer.flatten_candidates = True
2026-03-11T14:22:04.128Z DEBUG flattened_candidates = ['c1','c2','d1']
2026-03-11T14:22:04.130Z INFO scoring produced 3 scores
2026-03-11T14:22:04.131Z WARN candidate_to_query_mapping not recorded due to fast-path
```

ada: That fast-path skip is probably the culprit — scoring path assumed mapping persisted by the serializer, but the mapping was dropped when flattening happened in a separate codepath.

jordan: For triage: we need minimal repro from our side (unit test) and an immediate mitigation for customer. Can we ask them to send queries one at a time?

emma: Customer wants a fix, but they accepted a temporary workaround to run two calls and stitch results client-side. They asked for a postmortem.

liam: I'll reproduce locally with redwood-python/1.12.0. Quick repro python snippet:```python
import requests
body = {
  "queries": [
    {"qid": "q-1", "candidates": ["c1", "c2"]},
    {"qid": "q-2", "candidates": ["d1"]}
  ]
}
resp = requests.post('https://api.redwood.inference/v1/batch_rerank', json=body, headers={'Authorization':'Bearer x'})
print(resp.status_code, resp.text)
```

liam: Locally I can flip `serializer.flatten_candidates=False` and that yields a `scores_by_query` structure. With it set True I reproduce the ambiguous flattened response.

ops_oncall: From infra logs there's no OOM or spike; this is a correctness/serialization bug. Rolling a small hotfix to ensure `mapping` is always emitted even when flattening is used. I'll coordinate a patch against the 1.12.1 branch.

ada: QA will write a regression test to assert that the response contains either `scores_by_query` or an explicit `mapping` array of same length as scores.

support_bot: Inc created: INC-2026-345. Priority P2. Linked customer: Acme Health.

jordan: Next steps for support thread: 1) Offer workaround (call per-query) — done. 2) ETA for patch? ops_oncall / liam? 3) Ask customer to share any SDK wrappers they may have.

liam: ETA: small fix merged to branch, hotfix deploy scheduled in 2 hours to staging and 6 hours to production after smoke tests. Will provide PR link and changelog.

emma: Noted. I'll send the customer a clear explanation of what's happening and the workaround. Will update the incident ticket when prod deploy completes.

jordan: Thanks team. Add a note to release notes: "Fix: batch_rerank preserves per-query candidate mapping when flattening." :thumbsup:
